review_scope: Compared 23 installed candidate frames with the published main frames. Inspected Vantry’s silhouette in the occupied rooms and checked fixture surfaces, framing and light across the remaining views. Compared installed mesh and material records for the mail bank, watch station, fuse panel and radiator where reflections changed. This is a technical image review.

images.observation: The shorter rotors leave more shelving visible above Vantry. His eyes and grin read at the right edge. The table, pendant and coloured floor patch align across the pair.
The compact crown and wider expression are visible beside the bath. The lamp spot crosses the same tiles and the curtain keeps its vertical folds.
The resident, table and window keep their relative positions. Vantry’s fixed front plate is visible above the display and his case clears the resident’s face.
The shortened rotor silhouette stays below the window head in this framing. The shelving, table, window reflection and lit wall retain their shapes.
The lower rotor and front face clear the sink silhouette. The lamp pool is softer at the top in the candidate. The cabinet seams, worktop, taps and drain run remain visible.
The pressure gauge, dark firebox door, vertical piping and floor plate line up. The darker side wall retains its corner.
The chair and bookcase keep their outlines against the closed door. The tabletop catches a broader reflection in the candidate.
Tile joints meet at the same service corner. The bypass, hanger and vertical metal run remain distinct despite a change in reflected light.
Both views are very dark. Mortar courses and brick relief are visible in the same positions. The view provides little evidence about the mechanism.
The door and conduit are brighter in the candidate. The switches and instrument faces keep their positions. All 34 installed fuse-panel surface records match main.
The brass rail crosses the same dark booth opening. Foreground supports and floor tiles retain their spacing.
The orange and white figure, shelf edge and portrait remain legible against the dark green wall.
The narrow shelf silhouette and framed pictures sit below the same warm ceiling strip. This upward view shows little fine surface detail.
The brass mail fronts are brighter and flatter in this capture. Individual apertures, name cards and bench remain distinct. All 14 installed bank surface records match main.
Radiator fins and the valve sit below the same curtains beside the table. Reflections on the dial are lighter. All 33 installed radiator surface records match main.
Railing spacing, landing edges, door and ceiling conduit align. The upper landing remains distinct from the darker opening below.
The tank silhouette, cage, legs and parapet remain distinct against the same roofline and cloud bands.
The glass and green lamp remain legible in front of the workbench. The wood floor, board and table shadow keep their orientation.
The folded fitting, brackets and pipe curve sit against the same tiled corner. The seam along the fitting remains visible.
The coloured residue stays under the radiator in the amber lamp pool. Vantry’s casing and compact rotor stay clear of the centre of the effect.
The raised red forms remain individually visible against the radiator. The companion’s open date brow and larger face occupy the right margin.
The kettle handle, toaster slots, crumb tray and cups retain their silhouettes. Crumbs remain individually visible on the pale counter.
The wall has less reflected light and the right-hand fixture face is brighter in the candidate. The key and station window remain distinct. All 38 installed station surface records match main.
